name: Mitochondrial Myopathy with Reversible Cytochrome C Oxidase Deficiency
aliases: Reversible Cytochrome C Oxidase Deficiency Myopathy
Transient Cytochrome C Oxidase Deficiency Mitochondrial Myopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Reversible Cytochrome C Oxidase Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early-onset muscle weakness with hypotonia and delayed motor milestones
Muscle biopsy showing reversible cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficiency
Improvement or normalization of COX activity on follow-up biopsy or biochemical testing
Identification of mitochondrial DNA or nuclear gene mutations associated with reversible COX deficiency (if available)
Exclusion of other mitochondrial myopathies with permanent COX deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset muscle weakness with hypotonia plus muscle biopsy demonstrating reversible cytochrome c oxidase deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires demonstration of reversibility of COX deficiency, typically by follow-up biopsy or biochemical testing.

common.symptomName: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

occasional.symptomName: Ventilator dependence with inability to wean

laboratory: Elevated blood lactate and pyruvate levels during episodes
Normal or transiently decreased serum creatine kinase
Muscle biopsy showing reversible cytochrome c oxidase deficiency
imaging: Muscle MRI may show mild edema or signal changes during active phase
genetic: Mutations in mitochondrial DNA or nuclear genes affecting COX assembly or function (e.g., SCO2, SURF1) in some cases
other: Improvement or normalization of COX activity on follow-up muscle biopsy or biochemical testing

distinguishingFeatures: Permanent COX deficiency on muscle biopsy
Progressive clinical course without spontaneous improvement
Structural abnormalities on muscle biopsy without COX deficiency
Lack of reversibility of biochemical defects

differentialDiagnoses.diseaseId: mitochondrial encephalomyopathy lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS)

redFlags: Persistent lactic acidosis with metabolic decompensation
Lack of improvement or worsening COX deficiency on follow-up testing
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Kirby DM, et al. Reversible cytochrome c oxidase deficiency myopathy: a distinct mitochondrial disease. Neurology. 1999;52(3): 599-604.
Orphanet: Mitochondrial myopathy with reversible cytochrome C oxidase deficiency (ORPHA:254864)
